request.text: What is the voltage on C1?

solution.item: *** Solution by TINA assisted by AI ***
We know that generator frequency is f=100k Hz, w=2*pi*f
At first we calculate the total impedance between the generator nodes (Source)
L1 and R1 connected in series so Zb=j*w*L1+R1='636 / 81°'Ohm
C1 and Zb connected in series so Za=1/(j*w*C1)+Zb='968 / -84.1°'Ohm
Now we calculate the voltage on C1
We know that the voltage between Source nodes is '1 / -90°'V.
(1) The components C1,Zb connected in series.
(1) The voltage between this components starting and ending node is '1 / -90°'V.
(1) C1 is in the voltage divider so the voltage on C1 is 1/(j*w*C1)/Za*'1 / -90°'V = '1.64 / -95.9°'V.
